gaps.sentence: He was sent to ___ prison for armed robbery.
gaps.explanation: 'Be sent to prison' (as a prisoner) takes no article; visiting the building is 'go to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: She works in ___ insurance, not banking.
gaps.explanation: Industry/sector names take no article: in insurance, in banking, in marketing.

gaps.sentence: She's ___ MEP for the north-west region.
gaps.explanation: 'MEP' is pronounced /em iː piː/, so the vowel sound 'an' is required.

gaps.sentence: She works as ___ waitress during the summer holidays.
gaps.explanation: After 'as' and 'work as', jobs take a/an: work as a waitress.

gaps.sentence: ___ Sahara is expanding southwards by several kilometres a year.
gaps.explanation: Desert names take 'the': the Sahara, the Kalahari.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ excellent command of Japanese.
gaps.explanation: 'Have an excellent command of' — 'excellent' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: I saw ___ film last night, and the film was about mountain climbers.
gaps.hint: first mention of one of many
gaps.explanation: First mention of a countable noun takes 'a'; the second mention becomes 'the' (already written out here).
